<b>点差で考える。</b>2人対戦では「自分の点−相手の点」が大きいほど勝ちに: Think in point differences. In a two-player game, the bigger "your points − opponent's points" is, the closer you are to winning. A move that gains you 3 points is worth the same as one that denies your opponent 3. Handing your opponent 5 points is the same as losing 5 yourself.
<b>完成させると倍になる。</b>都市は完成すれば1タイル2点、未完成のまま終: Completing doubles the value. A completed city scores 2 per tile, an unfinished one only 1. A completed monastery scores 9; an unfinished one depends on how many neighbours are filled. Only roads score 1 per tile either way.
<b>ミープルは早く戻すほど得。</b>完成すればミープルは手元に戻り、また別の: The sooner a meeple returns, the better. When a feature is completed the meeple comes back and can score again somewhere else. Keeping your 7 meeples from getting stuck is the fastest way to raise your score.
最初の数ゲームは、この5つだけ意識すれば十分です。: For your first few games, these five are enough.
<b>小さな都市を作って、すぐ閉じる。</b>2〜3枚の都市は閉じやすく、確実に: Build small cities and close them quickly. Cities of 2–3 tiles are easy to close and reliably return points and meeples.
<b>道に乗せるのは、すぐ終わる道だけ。</b>道は安く、端が決まらないといつま: Only put meeples on roads that will end soon. Roads are cheap, and if the ends aren't fixed the meeple never comes back.
<b>修道院は、周りが埋まりやすい場所に。</b>盤の真ん中寄り、すでにタイルが: Put monasteries where the neighbours fill easily. Near the middle of the map, where there are already many tiles, they reach 9 points more easily.
<b>ミープルを1〜2個は手元に残す。</b>相手の都市に割り込む、終盤に農民を: Keep 1–2 meeples in hand. You can use them later for big plays, such as joining an opponent's city or placing farmers late in the game.
<b>置く前に「相手が得をしないか」を見る。</b>相手の都市を完成させてしまう: Before placing, check whether it helps your opponent. Completing their city gives them points and their meeple back. Compare your gain with theirs before you place.

<b>2人対戦では、相手が引くかもしれない。</b>合うタイルが残っていても、そ: In a two-player game, your opponent may draw it. Even if a fitting tile remains, your opponent will use it for themselves if they draw it. Treat holes with few fitting tiles as "almost never closing", and don't commit too many meeples to them.

新しい小さな都市を自分で始めて閉じる。: Start your own small cities and close them.
修道院は引いたら置きやすい場所へ。: When you draw a monastery, put it where it is easy to surround.
ミープルを一気に使い切らない。: Don't use up all your meeples at once.
相手の大きな都市に割り込んで分け合う。: Join your opponent's big city and share it.
自分の修道院の周りを自分で埋める。: Fill in around your own monastery yourself.
相手の都市の隣に、埋まりにくい穴ができる置き方を考える。: Look for placements that leave hard-to-fill holes next to your opponent's cities.
自分の都市は口を増やさず、早めに閉じる。: Don't add openings to your own cities; close them early.
<span class=\"when\">終盤（残り十数枚）</span>\n: End game (last dozen or so tiles) Cash in
もう閉じない都市や道に、新しくミープルを置かない。: Don't put new meeples on cities or roads that won't close in time.
余ったミープルは、完成した都市にたくさん接する草原へ。: Put spare meeples in fields that touch many completed cities.
修道院は未完成でも周りの数だけ点になる。: An unfinished monastery still scores for each neighbour.
最後の1枚まで、相手の完成を止める手を探す。: Keep looking for moves that stop your opponent completing things, right up to the last tile.

相手のミープルがいる都市には直接置けませんが、<b>すぐ隣に自分の小さな都市を作: You can't place directly in a city your opponent occupies, but you can start your own small city right next to it with a meeple, then connect the two with one tile. With equal meeples you both score in full; with more, only you score. The bigger their city, the more it is worth joining.
攻め：相手の都市を閉じにくくする: Attack: make your opponent's city hard to close

If you can create a hole no tile can fill, such as city · road · city · road, that city can never be completed. It drops from 2 points per tile to 1, and your opponent's meeple stays stuck until the end.
守り：割り込まれない・塞がれない都市にする: Defence: keep your cities from being joined or blocked
自分の都市の口は少なく保ち、閉じられるときに閉じる。大きく育てるほど、割り込みと: Keep few openings on your cities and close them when you can. The bigger a city grows, the bigger a target it becomes for joining and blocking.
相手が自分の都市の近くに別の都市を作り始めたら、割り込みの合図です。先に閉じるか: If your opponent starts another city next to yours, they are planning to join. Close yours first, or shape it so the two can't connect.
自分で3方向から都市が迫る穴を作らない。引けるタイルが少なくなります。: Don't create holes with city on three sides yourself. Few tiles will fit.
<b>草原は道と都市で区切られる。</b>道の両側は別々の草原です。農民を置く前: Fields are divided by roads and cities. The two sides of a road are separate fields. Before placing a farmer, check how far the field extends.
<b>完成しそうな都市にたくさん接する草原を選ぶ。</b>点になるのは終了時に完: Choose fields that touch many cities likely to be completed. Only cities completed by the end count, 3 points each. A field touching several small cities is a strong spot.
<b>草原も多数決。</b>都市と同じく、つながった草原では農民が多い人が点をも: Fields are decided by majority too. As with cities, in a connected field the player with more farmers scores, and with a tie both score in full. You can also join an opponent's big field from another field.
<b>農民は最後まで戻らない。</b>序盤に置きすぎると都市に使うミープルが足り: Farmers never come back. Place too many early and you'll run short of meeples for cities. One or two in the opening, the rest late.

都市・道・修道院・草原のこと。つながったものは1つの特徴として数える。: A city, road, monastery or field. Connected parts count as one feature.
都市のタイルについている紋章。完成した都市なら1つにつき2点増える。: The coat of arms on some city tiles. Each adds 2 points to a completed city.
都市や道の、まだタイルが置かれていない開いた辺。全部埋まると完成。: An open edge of a city or road with no tile next to it yet. When all are filled, the feature is complete.
別々に作った都市や草原をつないで、相手と同じ特徴に自分のミープルを入れること。: Connecting separately built cities or fields so your meeple shares a feature with your opponent's.
1つの特徴に複数のミープルがいるとき、多い人が点をもらう（同数なら全員満点）。: When one feature has several meeples, the player with the most scores (all tied players score in full).
どのタイルでも埋まらない穴があって、もう完成しない状態。: A feature with a hole no tile can fill, so it can never be completed.
